# Spook conditions

Use these in the new-style syntax: `condition: spook.<name>`, with fields under `options:` and the target under `target:`.

### `spook.chance`: Chance

Passes a set percentage of the time, chosen at random each check. Handy for adding a bit of variation to your automations.

Options:

- `percentage` (required, number, 0 to 100 %): How often this condition should pass, as a percentage. Example: `20`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#chance

### `spook.cooldown`: Cooldown

Passes only if this automation or script has not run within the given time (or has never run). A built-in cooldown, so it does not re-fire too often.

Options:

- `duration` (required, duration): How long to wait after the last run before this condition passes again. Example: `00:05:00`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#cooldown

### `spook.is_at_target_temperature`: Temperature at its target

Passes when the temperature of a thermostat or water heater is at its target. A device that is off is not at its target, and one that is unavailable is left out.

Target: `climate` or `water_heater` entities, or the devices, areas, floors and labels holding them.

Options:

- `behavior` (required, automation_behavior): Whether any of the devices being there is enough, or all of them have to be. Default: `any`.
- `tolerance` (optional, number, 0 to 10): How close to the target still counts as there, in the device's unit. For a thermostat that settles just short of its setpoint. Zero means the target itself. Default: `0`. Example: `0.5`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#temperature-at-its-target

### `spook.is_available`: Entity is available

Passes when an entity is there to talk to: anything but unavailable or unknown. For a speaker or a smart plug that is not always powered.

Target: any entities, devices, areas, floors or labels.

Options:

- `behavior` (required, automation_behavior): Whether any of the entities being there is enough, or all of them have to be. Default: `any`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#entity-is-available

### `spook.not_triggered_by_user`: Not triggered by a user

Passes when nobody can be held responsible for this run: a schedule, the sun, an integration acting on its own, or the Run button. Takes no options on purpose. To exclude specific people instead, put "Triggered by a user" inside a Not condition.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#not-triggered-by-a-user

### `spook.quota`: Run allowance left

Passes while this automation has run fewer than a given number of times within a given period. Scripts are not counted.

Options:

- `limit` (required, number, 1 to 64): How many runs are allowed within the period. Example: `5`.
- `period` (required, duration): The window the limit applies to. It rolls, so a day means any twenty-four hours rather than between midnights. Example: `24:00:00`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#run-allowance-left

### `spook.repair_issue_present`: Repair issue outstanding

Passes while a repair issue is outstanding. Issues somebody has ignored do not count.

Options:

- `domain` (optional, text, one or a list): Limit this to issues reported by particular integrations, by their domain. Leave it empty for all of them. Example: `hue`.
- `severity` (optional, list, each one of `critical`, `error`, `warning`): Limit this to issues of a particular severity. Leave it empty for all of them.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#repair-issue-outstanding

### `spook.triggered_by_automation`: Triggered by an automation

Passes when another automation set this run going, whether it did so directly or through a script.

Options:

- `automation` (optional, entity, one or a list): Limit this to particular automations. Leave it empty to accept any of them. Example: `automation.goodnight`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#triggered-by-an-automation

### `spook.triggered_by_user`: Triggered by a user

Passes when a person is behind what set this off: a state change or an event they caused, including one that made a template trigger become true. A schedule, the sun, or an integration acting on its own carries nobody, and neither does forcing a run with the Run button.

Options:

- `person` (optional, entity, one or a list): Only pass when one of these people started it. Leave empty to pass for anyone. A person has to have a user account linked to them, otherwise there is nothing to match against. Example: `person.frenck`.

Documentation: https://spook.boo/other-features#triggered-by-a-user
